clue.text: Attire to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the verb for boasting is written backwards

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: A dandy is told off for showing off about their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a synonym for clothing or dress, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Dogs in filthy places given bed inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for a bed goes within the word for filthy places

parts.note: sties are pigsties, proverbially filthy places
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Dogs kept in squalid kennels are at least given somewhere to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotties are Scottish terriers, a breed of small dog.

clue.text: Actress, I fancy, most likely to cause a fright

definitions.text: most likely to cause a fright

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a particular actress is the one most likely to scare an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like the verb 'I fancy' (I suppose), but it is the anagram signal on ACTRESS plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, describing whatever frightens most.

clue.text: Opponent has some important information

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An adversary is holding vital intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a noun is a person who is against something, an opposer.

clue.text: Greeting heard on a mountain maybe?

indicators.note: heard says the word for a greeting is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A hiker's hello rings out across the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up on a mountain is one example of being far above the ground, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Good inclination for work at harvest time

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: Being keen to help is a virtue when the crops come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaning is gathering leftover grain after the reapers, a harvest-time task.

clue.text: Plant guy found by lake

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A botanist's specimen was discovered by a fellow beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' reads as a man but is the verb meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a prickly plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Colour of little place that's clean on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the word for clean wraps round the short form for a place

parts.note: pure means clean or unsullied
PL is the short form of place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone asks what colour a small, tidy-looking spot is painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple is a colour between red and blue.

clue.text: Summary hard to understand

definitions.meaning: a short précis of a paper is called this
theoretical and difficult to follow, as abstruse ideas are

explanation.surface: A digest of a paper turns out to be impenetrable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a brief résumé and an adjective for abstruse, theoretical ideas.

clue.text: Enormous embrace offered with energy

parts.note: a hug is an embrace
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A massive cuddle is given with real vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge is a direct synonym of enormous, meaning extremely large.

clue.text: Returning prisoner keeps nothing in his institution

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards
keeps says the word for a prisoner holds the zero inside it

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in old lag
O stands for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A convict coming back has nothing to his name in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to the prisoner, making the definition fair: a gaol is the prisoner's institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaol, the British spelling of jail, is the institution where a prisoner is held.

clue.text: Amusing little creature seen by heather

parts.note: a tick is a tiny bloodsucking creature
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A small animal spotted in the heather is entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickling in the sense of entertaining or diverting, as when something tickles one's fancy.

clue.text: Shop you had with a number of floors

parts.note: a store is a shop
ye is an old form of you
D is the contraction of had, as in you'd

explanation.surface: A department store you once owned had several levels.
explanation.definitionFit: A building described as storeyed has a number of levels, as in a two-storeyed house.

clue.text: An exam they sat regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Students took an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an exam, a set of questions assessing knowledge.

clue.text: Record I have buried under vault

indicators.note: buried under says the contraction of I have goes below the vault, which in a down answer means after it

parts.note: an arch is a vault, a curved structure
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A buried document lies beneath an arched crypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical records, or as a verb, to file one away.

clue.text: Report of what may happen in maternity hospital bed

indicators.note: report of says the word is heard rather than seen, giving one that sounds alike

parts.words: what may happen in maternity hospital
parts.note: a birth is what takes place on a maternity ward

explanation.surface: News reaches us of a bed in the labour ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a bed or bunk on a ship or train.

clue.text: Instigate legal proceedings against woman

explanation.surface: Someone is taking a lady to court.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bring a lawsuit, and the same letters are a woman's name.

clue.text: At the scene of an event immediately

definitions.text: At the scene of an event
definitions.meaning: right where something happens, as a reporter on location

explanation.surface: A reporter is told to get to the incident without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both present at the place itself and at once, as in being sacked instantly.

clue.text: Coach or puff-puff? Hesitation

parts.note: puff-puff is a child's word for a steam train
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone dithers between two ways of travelling: bus or steam engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a vehicle alongside the train, but it is the definition: a person who trains athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a coach, someone who prepares athletes or teams.

clue.text: Public school said to be worried

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the school's name stands for a word that sounds like it

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A posh school is reported to be in a state of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten as in eaten up with worry, consumed by anxiety.

clue.text: Bitterness followed by a new attempt to establish polite respect

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: After a sour start, someone tries again to win courteous esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is courtly attentiveness and courtesy, especially towards women.

clue.text: Person who pays colonist

definitions.meaning: one who settles a bill or debt
someone who goes to live in a new land

explanation.surface: A pioneer turns out to be the one footing the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: One who settles an account, and also one who settles in a new country.

clue.text: Member finishes folk stories

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A club member brings tales of old to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends are traditional tales handed down among a people.

clue.text: It's most appropriate to imprison a cruel person

indicators.note: to imprison says the word for most appropriate locks the letter A inside it

parts.note: best means most suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: It is thought fitting to lock up someone vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a brutal or savage person, by extension from a wild animal.

clue.text: Lord's servant, explosive man in the Bible

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis

explanation.surface: A volatile biblical figure serves the Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' suggests God in a Bible surface, but the helots were serfs of Spartan masters.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf in ancient Sparta, bound to serve a master.

clue.text: Fish is not hot, having got left out

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from the word for not hot

parts.note: cold is the opposite of hot

explanation.surface: A fish has cooled down after being left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having got left out' reads as abandoned, but 'left' is L and 'out' removes it from COLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a common white-fleshed sea fish.
